candidates.original_title: Interruptibility of software developers and its prediction using psycho-physiological sensors
candidates.description: The original lab study claimed that biometric sensors can predict the interruptibility of software developers with high accuracy (91.5%) in a controlled lab environment.
candidates.citation_sentence: In this paper, we report on what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first external and close replication of the original lab study (Züger and Fritz 2015).
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly states it is an external close replication of the original lab study. The replication failed to replicate the original's high-accuracy classification results; models did not significantly outperform the majority classifier baseline. AQ5 was not replicated due to an incorrect post-interview questionnaire (noted in Section 6.4). The authors explicitly state they cannot replicate models that significantly improve over the majority classifier baseline. Severe threats to validity were identified: small sample size (10 participants), highly imbalanced dataset, and ad hoc transformation of the interruptibility scale. EDA features were dropped after sessions due to a measurement error (electrode saturation), which may have affected model performance.
